verdict.rationale: Fastmail's developer page says its API is JMAP per RFC 8620. JMAP's site advertises WebPush, which needs no permanent connection, so the server initiates delivery to a push endpoint. That is the closest the pack gets to an outbound callback a programmatic consumer could receive; the EventSource stream is client-held and does not count as a webhook. missing for 10: explicit Fastmail-side documentation of registering a callback URL (push subscription), event types and payload format, delivery, retry and verification semantics, and any independent or hands-on corroboration that Fastmail supports WebPush callbacks for non-mobile consumers.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can subscribe to events via webhooks

citations.quote: Or use WebPush for mobile-compatible push, no permanent connection required.
The JMAP session resource can be found at https://api.fastmail.com/jmap/session
